[00:00] Maya: hey everybody thanks for joining, we got about 45 minutes so we'll run through messaging, do two short demo runs and then Q&A. Ravi's gonna handle tech deep dive bits, lena will note any messaging gaps.

[01:08] Priyanka: kv-cache, yes that's key for us because we reuse prefixes a lot. how does that affect p99?
[01:15] Ravi: so in practice prefix/KV caching reduces token compute for repeated context, p50 improves a lot, p99 less predictable but we have fallbacks and routing. with dedicated pools you get more consistent p99 latency, hosted is more variable but cheaper overall.
[01:33] Maya: that's the core message: dedicated for strict SLOs and throughput guarantees; hosted for fast onboarding and cost efficiency.
[01:41] Sasha: curious, our security team will ask about SOC2 and KMS - do we have the docs?

[01:53] Maya: noted. (mumble) also mention audit logs and RBAC.
[02:00] Kyle: on private deployments, do you support air-gapped on-prem?
[02:04] Ravi: yes, private has on-prem option, control plane can be customer-managed in a VPC; caveat is certain managed features (like hosted analytics) need connectors. we'll surface tradeoffs in the doc.
[02:18] Tom: okay demo part, what's the demo scenario?
[02:22] Maya: we'll do a customer support assistant: 1) short turn chat showing streaming response and tool calls, 2) a longer context rerank/qa showing embeddings + rerank.
[02:33] Ravi: for the streaming piece i'll demonstrate real-time latency; note that demo env uses a small model variant to keep tokens cheap but we can talk about performance on larger quantized models.

[03:53] Tom: clients always ask about pricing - how to respond to latency vs cost tradeoffs?
[03:59] Lena: recommended script: ask about p95/p99 and peak QPS; propose dedicated if they need consistent p99 under high load, otherwise hosted plus caching/quantization. provide ballpark unit economics.
[04:13] Ravi: add specifics: batching helps throughput but adds latency headroom; for small chat workloads prefer small batch sizes and prefix cache. we'll show a slide with sample numbers.
[04:27] Maya: let's do a mock customer objection: "we can just use Vertex and autoscale instances" - Ravi?
[04:34] Ravi: respond: "Vertex gives infra, but Redwood is opinionated runtime + orchestration + developer DX; you get KV caching, fallback routing, optimized kernels, and observability tuned for model serving. it's about predictable unit cost and fewer surprises in production."
[04:53] Maya: nice. include a quick stat: median token cost reduction 20-40% vs naive serving (approx). don't cite as absolute.
